requirement: HF Operator Chat (HFCHAT) is an optional, simple chat between operators of nodes, one to one or to all; not a general purpose chat system.
HFCHAT clients exchange short text messages in the ITA5 (ASCII) character set.
An HFCHAT message is a character sequence ending with a carriage return and line feed pair (0x0D 0x0A).
An HFCHAT message, the CR LF included, is no longer than the subnetwork MTU.
notes: The MTU is the one in S_BIND_ACCEPTED.

requirement: How messages are displayed and entered is left to the implementation; the guidelines that follow are recommendations.
A client offers one common area for entering and displaying messages.
A client keeps a short viewable history of messages sent and received, the last N for an N between 10 and 100.
A client shows the source of each received message, for example the originator's node address.
A client shows the time each message was received.
notes: Page break: the item continues on O-2.

requirement: A client shows node delivery confirmation for messages it sends with the ARQ service.
A client offers both one to one and broadcast sending.
An HFCHAT client binds at SAP ID 5.
Message priority is configurable, and may be chosen by the operator.
The default message priority is 12.
A client may send with point-to-point or point-to-multipoint addressing.
Point-to-point defaults: ARQ, node delivery confirmation, in-order delivery.
Point-to-point messages go to the individual node address of the remote client.
Point-to-multipoint defaults: non-ARQ with a configurable number of repeats, no delivery confirmation, not in-order delivery.
notes: Default number of repeats: interp O-0024.

requirement: Point-to-multipoint messages go to the multicast address of the group; how a group gets its address is by procedure or out of band.
A client offers the option of the default broadcast address.
Characters are bit and byte aligned with the U_PDU octets, the character's LSB in the octet's LSB.
The unused eighth bit (MSB) of each octet is zero.
One message per S_Primitive, the terminating CR LF as the last two octets of the U_PDU.

The default number of repeats for point-to-multipoint messages is NOT STATED; only that it is configurable. Reading: the client asks for a minimum of 1 retransmission (S_UNIDATA_REQUEST MinRetx 1, S-0084) unless configured otherwise.

What a client does with a received U_PDU that is not a valid HFCHAT message (no CR LF at the end, a non-ASCII or control octet) is NOT STATED. Reading: show it anyway, the final CR LF dropped if present and any octet that is not printable ASCII shown as a question mark.

The service type of the HFCHAT bind is NOT STATED; only the defaults per addressing mode (O-0016, O-0018). Reading: bind with ARQ (the point-to-point default) and send every message with an explicit delivery mode, so a group message is never sent ARQ (which the node rejects, interp S-0138).
